takeaway: Keep moving, start with what you can do, and build from there. We'll continue building your toolbox.
why: Understand why movement is part of treatment, not just something added at the end.

slides.title: Why we keep you moving
slides.content: Movement is how we rebuild strength, activity tolerance, and confidence. Muscles need practice to meet the demands of walking, lifting, work, and everyday life. Over time, a suitable amount of activity can help you do more.

slides.title: Experience matters too
slides.content: If an activity has been uncomfortable, it can feel uncertain to try it again. A manageable experience gives you something concrete to learn from: what you could do, how you responded, and what to adjust next time. Confidence can grow through that practice.

slides.title: The hands-on treatment is one piece of the puzzle
slides.content: Hands-on care may help things settle and make movement more comfortable. When it does, that creates an opportunity to practise. It does not mean you must have treatment before you can move, or that every visit will produce the same response.

slides.title: Keep moving
slides.content: Start with what you can do, and build from there. A walk, an exercise, or an ordinary activity can be part of that. The starting point should fit your current ability and any restrictions or guidance from your assessment.

slides.title: Discomfort needs context
slides.content: Some familiar discomfort can occur during activity without meaning you have caused new damage. Look at how you function and how symptoms settle as well as how it feels in the moment. If the response is repeatedly more than expected, adjust or seek advice. New or concerning changes need assessment.

slides.title: Use what we practised
slides.content: Choose one activity from your plan and a manageable amount. Notice how it feels during and afterwards. The aim is not to prove you can push through; it is to build experiences you can learn from and gradually return to the things you enjoy.
